British Values
In accordance with the Department for Education we aim to actively promote British values in school to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encourages to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right ‘ and ‘wrong’ all people living in the UK are subject to its law. The Key British Values are;
democracy
rule of law
individual liberty
mutual respect

pageCache.text:
A Warm Welcome To Our Website
Welcome to our school website, we hope you find it informative and useful. “Every Child, Every Chance, Every Day”
At Walton CEVC Primary School we aim to provide a safe, caring, happy and stimulating learning environment where everyone’s contribution is valued. All the members of our school community are encouraged to develop their full potential. We work as a team to provide a balanced and relevant curriculum, where all the children experience equal access to learning and all individual needs are met. We believe that all children should have the opportunity to build their confidence and self-esteem. Celebrating success and effort in all aspects of school life are essential features of our school. It is vital to equip our children with all the skills necessary for them to become thoughtful, hardworking, considerate and well-motivated citizens of the future as they move through primary school and onto the secondary phase of their education. Our OFSTED inspection in October 2023 found….“The school has planned a broad and ambitious curriculum. They adapt the curriculum appropriately for the mixed aged classes… In Reception, children begin to learn numeracy and literacy as soon as they start. The school plans activities and play to support children’s interest…The school ensures that teachers have bespoke training to support SEND pupils. This means teachers skilfully adapt the curriculum to support these pupils…Pupils are calm and orderly, both in the classroom and out… Pupils are positive about their learning…The school ensures there is a well-planned personal, social and health education curriculum. This begins in early years…They are well prepared for life in modern Britain…Parents are enthusiastic about the school. The school culture is safe and nurturing. This encourages pupils to develop their confidence, for example learning new musical instruments or singing to the parents and community…Pupils are proud of their school. They show care and consideration for one another.” It is very important for prospective parents to visit our school to assess the learning opportunities we offer and experience the atmosphere of Walton CEVC Primary School. To arrange a visit please contact Mrs Sweet, our office manager, on 01458 443675. We look forward to meeting you and your children. Yours faithfully,
Lucas Upham Mr David Hatrey Headteacher Chair of Governors

Parent Teachers Association (PTA)
Welcome to Walton Primary School PTA
The Walton Primary School Parent Teacher Association (PTA) brings together parents, carers and school staff to support our school and help make our children’s time at Walton as enjoyable and enriching as possible.
Every parent and carer is welcome to get involved. Whether you have lots of time, an occasional hour to spare, a great idea or simply want to support our events, every contribution makes a difference. 2026 text to update
Being part of the PTA is a great way to become more involved in school life, meet other parents and carers, share your ideas and skills and help make a positive difference for our children.
And getting involved doesn't have to mean a big commitment.
You might join the committee, help at an event, bake a cake, source a raffle prize, share a fundraising idea or simply come along and support an activity. You can help regularly, once a term, once a year or whenever you have some spare time.
However you choose to get involved, we'd love to have you!
Our PTA committee is made up of parent and carer volunteers who give their time to help organise events, fundraising and projects for the school.
Co-Chairs: Jo Linter & Allison O'Regan Treasurer: Charlotte Daborn Secretary: Vacancy – could you help?
Ordinary Committee Members
Lucy Davies Rachel Ashman Lian Hardware Emily Milson Karen Doble Hywel Thomas Hannah Phillips Naomi Johnson Steliana Parsons Karl Shoemark
Committee roles are reviewed and appointed at our Annual General Meeting (AGM) which will usually be held at the start of the academic year in September/October.
We elect the officers of the committee annually (Chair, Treasurer and Secretary), but welcome ordinary members to join at any time. Find out about the roles here: Chair Treasurer Secretary Ordinary Committee Member
What Your PTA Support Makes Possible
Thanks to the fantastic support of our families, staff and wider community, during 2025/26 the PTA raised £3,258.74 and invested £6,292.58 in projects, resources and experiences for the school.
PTA funding helped support:
Together, we make a difference!
We want to continue working closely with the school to identify where PTA funding can make the greatest difference, including further outdoor development and new classroom resources.
We also welcome support from parents, carers, local businesses and members of our wider community who may be able to offer resources, materials, equipment, expertise, advice or services. PTA Newsletter September 2026
Have an idea? We'd love to hear it.
Our School Lottery is an easy way to support Walton CEVC Primary School throughout the year, with the chance to win too.
Tickets cost £1 per week, with proceeds helping raise money for the school. One of our players wins a cash prize every week, with the possibility of winning the £25,000 jackpot.
JOIN OUR SCHOOL LOTTERY NOW - www.yourschoollottery.co.uk/lottery/school/walton-cevc-primary-school
You can also raise money for the PTA without it costing you anything extra when shopping online.
The PTA is registered with easyfundraising, where participating retailers make a donation when supporters shop through the service.
SUPPORT US WITH EASYFUNDRAISING here - https://www.easyfundraising.org.uk/causes/walton-primary-school-pta
There are parent/carer WhatsApp groups for each class or year group. These groups are independently run by parents and are a useful way to connect with other families, share reminders and keep up with school and PTA activities.
If you're not yet connected to your group, speak to a PTA member and we'll help point you in the right direction.
You can also join the Walton School Parents Facebook group, where families can connect and we share PTA event information and reminders.
We'd Love You to Get Involved
We're always pleased to hear from people who would like to:
You don't need previous PTA experience or any particular skills. Enthusiasm, ideas and a willingness to help are more than enough.
Email: waltonprimaryschoolpta@gmail.com
Come and say hello at one of our events, speak to a committee member in the playground or send us an email. We'd love to hear from you.
Together, we can continue making a difference for all the children at Walton Primary School.

Phonics and Reading
At Walton C of E Primary School, we use the Read Write Inc. phonics programme to teach our children to read, spell and write. The National Curriculum for Phonics aims to ensure that all pupils:
• In Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) and key stage one (KS1) are given the best opportunity to achieve expected progress, or more, in reading.
• To create an inclusive, inspired and challenging curriculum which develops children’s knowledge of phonics, enabling them to become successful, confident readers, who develop a life-long love of reading.
• Children will be able to apply their phonic knowledge to confidently spell many words either correctly or phonetically using the sounds they have learnt. They will know spelling alternatives for different sounds and be able to apply these consistently.
We want children to learn to read fluently, accurately and confidently. We know that reading is the key that unlocks the whole curriculum and enables them to access their learning. Therefore, the ability to decode efficiently is essential. We also want children to see reading not only as a task set by teachers in school, as part of the curriculum but as an activity which provides pleasure and escape from the modern world.

pageCache.text:
Children Looked After
At Walton C of E Primary School, we are very proud of the work we do with children of all backgrounds and needs. We recognise the importance of supporting pupils who may currently be a Child Looked After or Post Looked After. Our staff have up to date training and recent experience of working well with Looked After Children.
The Designated Lead for Children Looked After is: Mrs Cooper.
Pastoral support for pupils is provided by our School Elsa's: Mrs Tina Brine and Mrs Harriet Chinnock.
All staff have training which includes how to support children who are looked after, Special Guardianship or Adopted. This training includes a broad understanding of attachment, building trust and providing a safe and secure environment for a successful school experience.
We work very closely with parents, foster parents, carers and professionals to ensure that children's personal needs are met. If your child is looked after, under a Special Guardianship or Adopted, please do speak to staff about this.
